operating_rules: Skills are organized collections of files packaging procedural knowledge for agents, not just prompts
Skills have 3 layers: (1) description (helps Claude identify when to use it), (2) instructions (detailed steps), (3) examples (real use cases)
Two effective engineer archetypes: hyper-specialists (deep domain mastery like dev tools/JavaScript runtimes) and hyper-generalists (span product + design/research/business, unorthodox thinking)
In production environments, Agent Builder provides more control than GPTs via node-based workflows instead of single prompts
Always decide in plans whether code is overengineered, underengineered, or perfectly engineered and document why

specific_tactics: In Agent Builder: set output format to JSON with schema to create variables classified from agent response (e.g., product return, info request, purchase)
Use web search tool in agents with optional params: specific website domain crawl, user location filtering for localized results
Attach chat kit widgets (weather, e-commerce, event reminders, calendar) to agent conversations for interactive UI without code
Use code interpreter node to run Python scripts for data manipulation and graph visuals
Enable message actions in agent preview: thumbs up/down for feedback loops, retry button for response refinement
prompts: To identify skills worth creating: 'What recurring, multi-step tasks am I doing manually that could be abstracted as a reusable skill?'
Agent Builder system instruction structure: start with role definition, add task scope, include style/tone directives, specify output format
skills: Skill architecture (Claude Code): description layer (clear folder label for auto-detection), instructions layer (step-by-step procedural logic), examples layer (real-world use cases for context)
gates: Agent output format validation: JSON schema definition before connecting downstream nodes to prevent type mismatches
Evaluation gate in Agent Builder: set criteria (agent politeness, accuracy), run stress tests on workflows, catch conversation failures
Code quality gate (implied): test arbitrary tool, verify functionality works, then ask agent to write its own implementation
content_ideas: How to build a customer service agent in Agent Builder using return/purchase decision branches and chat kit widgets

Hyper-specialist vs hyper-generalist career paths in AI engineering: specialization depth (dev tools) vs weird/unorthodox thinking (cross-domain product leverage)
